marks.quote: Q3: registry goes to beta with three partner districts
marks.note: The whole quarter's deliverable list, stated explicitly with owners implied per item.

marks.quote: The registry beta has to come first because everything else demos on top of it, then the reviewer, then the needs board, then labels, then insights.
marks.note: A full sequence with a stated rationale for the ordering.

marks.quote: The needs board doesn't actually depend on the registry beta. I could ship it earlier and it'd de-risk the access story for the fundraiser.
marks.note: Disagreement voiced in the same meeting the sequence was proposed, not in the hallway afterward.

marks.quote: The needs board doesn't actually depend on the registry beta.
marks.note: An observable dependency fact stated first; the conclusion (ship earlier) drawn from it second.

marks.quote: Maybe, but I'd rather keep the demo coherent. Let's hold the sequence.
marks.note: The turn metadata flags this as an interruption: it starts 1.5s before Rachel's turn ends.

marks.quote: I'll flag the same thing I flagged in the retro — that was a decision made fast without much room for the objection.
marks.note: A peer naming the lead's pattern, to the lead, in the room.

marks.quote: Rachel just gave you new information and the sequence didn't move.
marks.note: Observation stated as fact before any conclusion; no motive attributed.

marks.quote: I'm doing the thing again, aren't I.
marks.note: Unprompted admission of the named pattern, mid-meeting, by the most senior person in the room.

marks.quote: Rachel, if the needs board is independent, pull it forward.
marks.note: Accepts the correction without counter-argument and states the change: the sequence moves.

marks.quote: You caught it in the same meeting though. That's the improvement.
marks.note: Specific positive feedback delivered seconds after the behavior it names.

marks.quote: I'll take that one — it's adjacent to the access needs-board and credits broker anyway.
marks.note: Ownership named in the room, so the action item does not float.

marks.quote: Quick clarifier — who owns the follow-up here, and by when?
marks.note: The ownership decision existed only by implication until this asked for it out loud.

marks.quote: Alright, let me read back the action items so we're aligned before we drop.
marks.note: Decisions restated at close to confirm shared understanding.

marks.quote: I'll capture the specifics in the notes.
marks.note: Follow-ups assigned with owners but no stated outcome, standard, or date; the 'done' criteria are deferred to notes that this meeting never sees.

uncoded.quote: One concern and then I'll drop it: are we sure about the sequencing here?
uncoded.note: Recurs four times in this meeting across three speakers: a concern raised while pre-committing to abandon it. Matches no code in the book. Candidate new code for CONFLICT / Surfacing Disagreement, negative valence, per the spec's uncoded-observation rule.

uncoded.quote: That's the plan. I've thought through the sequencing and I think it's right.
uncoded.note: A decision presented as settled before reactions are invited. Reads as commitment-suppressing, but no code in the book names it. Second candidate.

not_codable: Dana holding 66.2% of content speech is this meeting's loudest signal and no single utterance codes for it. Dominance is an aggregate: it belongs to PRD 05's metric contract, which is the other half of this page. The codebook and the metric contract are complements, not rivals.
